title: Correction Effort Is the Missing Spec
stat: 74 percent of research teams now run an AI step inside synthesis, up from 41 percent two years ago
source: A cross-vendor survey of research operations leads
topic_claim: the practice of treating survey provenance as settled is now the field's default answer
story_examples: One agent scanned four hundred papers and chose the twelve that counted as sources.
Another ranked a season of interview notes by strategic fit against our scoring sheet.
A third drafted the synthesis report before anyone opened the raw quote file.
thesis: Every fix costs more than it should because nothing tracks which claim a correction touched. Corrections matter less than correction effort, the time a fix costs a reader who wants to disagree. The fix queue is where that cost gets paid, one note at a time
design_moves: require the source quote next to every fixed line
review the fix instead of the document
counter: the fixed-boundary story no longer matches what agent pipelines and their silent defaults actually allocate
definition: Correction effort is the work a reader must spend to push a claim back toward its evidence
gap_stat_a: 68 percent of teams say corrections decide their trust in a report
gap_stat_b: only 22 percent can show where a correction landed
takeaway: Write the filter you would want run on you: expose rationale, log the cut, show the raw.
question_tail: Which step in your pipeline still claims survey provenance it cannot show?
person_context: I have shipped agent pipelines for two years
